title: How do we mark five fractions of our own choice?
description: Five fractions of our own choice are marked on a number line. The board takes one fraction, cuts the unit into the bottom number of equal parts, counts the top number of parts from zero, repeats for four more and checks each count.
teaching_notes: One idea: any fraction is marked by cutting the unit into as many equal parts as the bottom number and counting as many parts as the top number. Watch for students who count the marks instead of the parts.

video_script.why: A learner marks any chosen fraction on the number line by cutting the unit and counting parts.
video_script.substitution: five fractions chosen by the learner; the video shows one set of five
video_script.anchor: a number line from 0 to 1 cut into equal parts
video_script.payoff_line: Five fractions marked are one fourth, three fourths, two thirds, five sixths and seven eighths

final_answer.spoken: one fourth, three fourths, two thirds, five sixths and seven eighths

video_script.fraction_reading: one fourth, three fourths, two thirds, five sixths, seven eighths
maths_rules: 3/4: cut 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts and count 3 parts from 0
1/4: 4 equal parts, count 1; 2/3: 3 equal parts, count 2
5/6: 6 equal parts, count 5; 7/8: 8 equal parts, count 7
answers vary: any fraction works if the cut is the bottom number and the count is the top number
video_script.design: One number line from zero to one, cut again for each chosen fraction. Three fourths is the model; the other four follow the same cut and count.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>We choose five fractions of our own.
<bookmark mark='boxes'/>Then we mark each one on the number line.
How can we mark any fraction we choose?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='bottom'/>The bottom number of a fraction tells how many equal parts the unit has.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top number tells how many of those parts to count from zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: any 5 fractions of our choice
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, we may choose any five fractions.

beats.on_screen: To do: mark the 5 fractions on the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to mark the five fractions on the number line.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: choose 3/4; cut 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts

marks.pick: the fraction 3/4 is written in the first box
marks.cut: the unit from 0 to 1 is cut into four equal parts

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>Step one, we use the same way as the example in your book. Choose a fraction, for example three fourths.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>The bottom number is four, so cut the unit into four equal parts.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the top number is 3, so count 3 parts from 0 and mark the place

marks.count: three parts are counted from 0 and a mark is drawn at the end of the third

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, the top number is three. Count three parts from zero and mark the place.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: four more fractions; cut into 4, 3, 6 and 8 equal parts; count 1, 2, 5 and 7 parts

marks.more: four more number lines appear, cut into four, three, six and eight equal parts

narration: <bookmark mark='more'/>Step three, repeat for four more fractions. Cut the unit into four, three, six and eight equal parts. Count one, two, five and seven parts.

beats.on_screen: Check: each mark is as many parts from 0 as its top number

marks.check: each mark is traced back to 0 and its parts are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, count back from each mark to zero. The number of parts must be the top number.

beats.on_screen: Answer (answers vary): 1/4, 3/4, 2/3, 5/6, 7/8 marked on their number lines

marks.ans: the five fractions are written in the five boxes
marks.vary: the words answers vary appear beside the boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five fractions marked are one fourth, three fourths, two thirds, five sixths and seven eighths.
<bookmark mark='vary'/>Your own five can differ, if you cut and count the same way.
